chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:

He was asked about a man who died and left a son who did not know whether his father had performed Hajj or not. He said: 'The son should perform Hajj on his behalf. If his father had already performed Hajj, an optional (Hajj) is recorded for the father, and an obligatory (Hajj) for the son. And if his father had not performed Hajj, an obligatory (Hajj) is recorded for the father, and an optional (Hajj) for the son.'

key_terms.يَحُجُّ عَنْهُ: he performs Hajj on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a son performs Hajj for his father but doesn't know if the father already performed his obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the Shia principle of 'vicarious performance' (al-hajj 'an al-mayyit), where a single act of worship can simultaneously fulfill the obligatory duty for the deceased and the voluntary merit for the living agent. The Imam’s explanation resolves the uncertainty of the father's status by attributing the reward of 'fard' (obligatory) to the one who lacked it and 'nafl' (voluntary) to the one who already possessed it, ensuring no spiritual loss for either party. This reflects the broader Shia juristic view that Hajj can be performed by proxy for the deceased, a practice rooted in the Prophet's tradition and elaborated by the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>

was asked about a man who died and for him was a son who did not know whether his father had performed Hajj or not’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should perform Hajj on his behalf. So if it was such that his father had performed Hajj, an optional (Hajj) would be Written for his father, and for the son, the Obligatory (Hajj); and if it was such that his father had not performed Hajj, an Obligatory (Hajj) would be Written for his father, and for the son, the optional (Hajj)’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who dies and has a son who does not know if his father has performed al-Hajj or not. He (the Imam) said, ‘He performs al-Hajj on his behalf, if his father has performed al-Hajj, it is written as optional al-Hajj for him and an obligatory al-Hajj for his son; and if his father has not performed al-Hajj, it is written obligatory for his father and optional for the son.’”
